story: Alex checked the stove three times, even though the kettle hadn’t been on for ten minutes. Each time, his hand hovered over the cool metal, a small jump in his chest accompanying the motion. He rearranged the fruit bowl, separating the apples by shade, then by size, then back again. A persistent tightness had settled in his shoulders, making him want to shrug constantly, but he kept them rigidly still. The chipped mug felt strangely fragile in his grip as he carried his tea to the window, needing to see the predictable rhythm of the street to feel…settled. He traced the condensation with a fingertip, a small, repetitive circle.

Alex checked the stove three times before leaving, even though breakfast had been hours ago. The chipped ceramic of his favorite mug felt slick in his hands as he rinsed it, a small tremor running through his fingers. He rearranged the books on the shelf, aligning their spines with obsessive precision, then immediately stepped back to assess the symmetry. Outside, the mail carrier’s truck sounded like an approaching storm, and Alex found himself holding his breath until it passed. He double-locked the door, patted his pockets for his keys, then checked the lock again, a tightness building in his chest with each repetition.

Alex checked the stove three times, even though the kettle hadn’t been on for ten minutes. A tightness settled in his chest with each glance, a small bird fluttering against his ribs. He smoothed the already-smooth tablecloth, then rearranged the fruit bowl by color, a pointless task he repeated until the apples and oranges formed a perfect gradient. His friend, Ben, was due any minute, and Alex found himself replaying their last conversation, searching for any hint of disapproval in his tone. He kept glancing at the window, a cold prickle rising on the back of his neck with every passing car. Each breath felt shallow, insufficient.
